subject.title: feat(memory): add excludePaths option to memorySearch config

question: Should OpenClaw ship a builtin-only public `memorySearch.excludePaths` config key after the matcher repair, or should exclusion scope wait for QMD and broader recall/index eligibility design?
rationale: The code defect is mechanical, but the permanent product boundary is a new public memorySearch config key that is explicitly unsupported by QMD today.

options.title: Ship builtin-only after matcher repair
options.body: Fix pattern normalization, keep the QMD caveat in docs/help, and let a follow-up handle QMD or recall eligibility parity.

options.title: Require QMD parity first
options.body: Hold this PR until the same exclusion semantics are designed and tested for QMD indexing.

options.title: Fold into broader path-scope design
options.body: Pause or supersede this PR in favor of the broader recall/index eligibility work tracked at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/101422.

recommendation.title: Ship builtin-only after matcher repair
recommendation.body: Fix pattern normalization, keep the QMD caveat in docs/help, and let a follow-up handle QMD or recall eligibility parity.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses memory indexing, config compatibility, and docs, where steipete has the strongest recent history in the affected files.
